meta.note: written eight weeks into 2026 from the standings, the all-play Elo, the season simulation's odds, each roster's WAR pace (banked plus the rest of the projection, best legal lineup, taxi and IR excluded), and every trade since the preseason outlooks

8.head: 6-2 · Elo 1692 (1st) · WAR pace +9.11 (1st) · playoffs 99.97% · title 43%
8.text: Let's not overreact to two losses. Fine, let's overreact a little. The Church won its first six games by an average of 47 points, then dropped back-to-back games to Jeantrification and Drake Mungo, the second one with Zay Flowers posting a donut. That's not a collapse, that's the '86 Celtics losing a random game in January. This is still first in points, first in Elo, first in WAR pace, 89% for a bye and 43% for the title, twelve points clear of anyone else. Brock Bowers and CeeDee Lamb lead the roster with 0.77 WAR banked apiece. The flaw is the same one from August: no first or second until 2029, so the bench is the insurance policy. And the bench is holding Jayden Daniels, on pace for 0.86 WAR, like a guy keeping a winning lottery ticket in his sock drawer while Chase Brown plays flex on pace for 0.57. Cash the ticket. Turn Daniels into a real flex and this goes from favorite to prohibitive favorite.

2.head: 6-2 · Elo 1653 (3rd) · WAR pace +8.30 (2nd) · playoffs 99.4% · title 31%
2.text: Four trades in thirteen days. When Davante Adams and Mike Evans, the two 33-year-olds holding down the WR2 and WR3 seats, both landed on IR, the front office went full Danny Ainge at the deadline with a burner phone. DJ Moore, Jakobi Meyers, Geno Smith and Devaughn Vele came in for spare parts, a 2029 second and a couple of later picks. Then the big one: Lamar Jackson, who lasted one snap in Week 8, went to Baby Billys the same weekend for Trevor Lawrence and a 2027 second. Lawrence is on pace for 1.15 WAR. If Lamar's one-snap Sunday turns into anything longer, that's a heist. The engine is still Bijan Robinson (on pace for 1.39 WAR) and Christian McCaffrey (1.29), good for second in WAR pace and 99.4% playoff odds. The bill: 231 points left on the bench, Travis Kelce at 36 in the flex, and Saquon Barkley on the bench on pace for 0.20 WAR, which still beats Brian Thomas, the guy he cost, at -0.56. Two firsts left, 2028 and 2029. This roster has a sell-by date, and it's printed in January.

11.head: 6-2 · Elo 1580 (5th) · WAR pace +6.91 (5th) · playoffs 79% · title 2%
11.text: Four straight wins, and the last three opponents scored 71, 72 and 60. I'm not saying it's a fraud. I'm saying the schedule printed half of this record. Sixth in points for, fifth in Elo, fifth in WAR pace, and the sim gives it 79% for the playoffs and a 2% title shot, the worst odds of the three 6-2 teams by a mile. The real thing here is Jaxon Smith-Njigba, on pace for 2.02 WAR, the best of any player in the league. The best move was selling Jalen Hurts and a second for Tyler Shough and a third: Hurts is now on IR on somebody else's roster and Shough is on pace for 0.84 WAR. Naming the team after him is the fantasy version of a tattoo on the third date, but fine. The worst thing is 279 points left on the bench, second most in the league, with Keenan Allen at 34 as the WR3 and Terry McLaurin on IR. The 2028 and 2029 firsts are untouched. Spend one on a receiver, because the December opponents won't all score 60.

6.head: 5-3 · Elo 1660 (2nd) · WAR pace +8.23 (3rd) · playoffs 96% · title 17%
6.text: Here's the team nobody wants to see in December. Jeantrification beat the Church in Week 7, hung 168 on Bijan al-Gaib in Week 8, and sits second in Elo, third in WAR pace and third in points. Puka Nacua (on pace for 1.35 WAR), Tee Higgins and Christian Watson make three real receivers, which is three more than Hampton Inn has. Bucky Irving, bought for a 2028 first, is on pace for 0.78 WAR and earning it. Then there's the injury report, which reads like the closing credits of a war movie: Dak, Kittle, Irving, Rashee Rice, Ladd McConkey, Quinshon Judkins and Daniel Jones all carry tags, and De'Von Achane is done for the year. That's how you leave 282 points on the bench, the most in the league. You can't control hamstrings. You can control the lineup. The sim says 96% for the playoffs and 17% for the title, third behind the two teams it just beat. There's no Achane cavalry coming, so the upgrade has to come from the lineup decisions or a trade. Get those right and 17% is too low.

1.head: 5-3 · Elo 1615 (4th) · WAR pace +6.94 (4th) · playoffs 75% · title 4%
1.text: At 2-3 the board called this the best losing team in the league. Since then Drake Mungo has won four straight by an average of 62 points, capped by a 152-110 beatdown of the Church. Trey McBride is on pace for 1.56 WAR, the best tight end season in the league, and the quarterback room is so deep that Kirk Cousins has banked 0.71 WAR as the third guy behind Brock Purdy and Drake Maye. The receivers are the problem. A.J. Brown, who cost the 2027 first, is below replacement for the season. Justin Jefferson has banked 0.19 WAR, and Drake London and DK Metcalf just combined for 3.2 points. That's a lot of name recognition for not a lot of points. Fourth in Elo, fourth in WAR pace, 75% for the playoffs. A team this loaded at quarterback and tight end with this little at receiver is a Cousins trade waiting to happen. Make the call.

10.head: 5-3 · Elo 1519 (7th) · WAR pace +6.01 (7th) · playoffs 57% · title 1%
10.text: Remember 4-0? The Nix pics do, fondly, like a guy who peaked in high school. It's 1-3 since, the Week 8 loss to Homie G knocked 28 points off the playoff odds, and the sim now has it at 57% to get in and 1% to win it. Seventh in Elo, seventh in WAR pace, seventh in points. Seventh is the whole personality. Kyren Williams (on pace for 1.09 WAR) and Derrick Henry, still rolling at 32, are a real backfield. The receivers are Garrett Wilson, Parker Washington and Jaylen Waddle, who is below replacement for the season. Brandon Aiyuk is a DNR, Deebo Samuel is on IR with four friends, and Bo Nix and Tucker Kraft are questionable. One trade all season, back in Week 1, while the rest of the league runs a swap meet. And the 2027 first already belongs to Tyson chicken tenders, so there's no tank to fall back on. Use the 2028 first on a receiver, or accept that 4-0 was the movie and this is the straight-to-streaming sequel.

3.head: 5-3 · Elo 1452 (8th) · WAR pace +5.09 (8th) · playoffs 35% · title 0.7%
3.text: The cockroach of the league, and I mean that as a compliment. The last outlook had this as a 12% playoff team and said stop spending on this season. Since then: four straight wins, a 2027 third for Romeo Doubs (already on IR, because of course he is) and 35% playoff odds. I love it. I don't trust it. Eighth in points, eighth in Elo, eighth in WAR pace. Kenneth Walker is on pace for 1.44 WAR, fifth-best in the league, and carrying everybody. Then there's the superflex, where 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers scored 4.9 points in Week 8 while Cam Ward put up 25.3 on the bench. Rodgers was the right call on paper. At some point the paper loses. Here's the part that changes the math: the 2027 first belongs to These Bitches Love 'Doza, so missing the playoffs buys nothing, and Bijan al-Gaib's first lands late. There's no reason to hold back. Play Ward, ride Walker and see how long the cockroach lives.

9.head: 3-5 · Elo 1572 (6th) · WAR pace +6.65 (6th) · playoffs 34% · title 2%
9.text: The unluckiest team in the league, and it isn't close. Fifth in points, sixth in Elo, sixth in WAR pace, the fewest points left on the bench of anyone, and 3-5, with the last three losses by 8, 2 and 24. This is the guy at the blackjack table who plays every hand by the book while the dealer keeps pulling 21. Jahmyr Gibbs is on pace for 2.00 WAR, second in the league, and D'Andre Swift is on pace for 0.97. The quarterbacks are the leak: Matthew Stafford at 38, Michael Penix questionable and on pace for 0.40 WAR, Justin Herbert parked on the bench. The sim still gives this 34%, which tells you the roster is better than the record. And nobody in the hunt has more ammo: every own first through 2029, plus three extra seconds. Buy a quarterback this week. Losing close games with Stafford is how you end up 6-8 telling people about your point differential.

7.head: 3-5 · Elo 1392 (9th) · WAR pace +3.78 (9th) · playoffs 26% · title 0.3%
7.text: Two of the best quarterbacks in the league and nothing else. It's owning two Ferraris and no road. Josh Allen is on pace for 1.73 WAR, the best quarterback season in the league, and Joe Burrow, second-best at 1.32 WAR, just dropped 39.5 points to beat Captain Jah'Merica as a 30% underdog. The other seven lineup seats combine for about 0.7 WAR of pace. Total. The last outlook said sell one of the quarterbacks. Nothing happened. So now it's 3-5, ninth in points, ninth in Elo, with 26% playoff odds, which is exactly enough hope to keep making the wrong decision. Worse, the 2027 first belongs to These Bitches Love 'Doza, so there's no reward for losing either. This is the worst spot in fantasy football: not good enough to win, not bad enough to benefit, and not even holding your own pick. Allen at 30 will never be worth more than he is right now. Sell him to a contender and buy the receivers this lineup has never had.

4.head: 2-6 · Elo 1297 (11th) · WAR pace +0.86 (11th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
4.text: Here's where it gets weird. The last outlook called this a teardown on schedule, and then the teardown went shopping. Tyler Shough and a third went out for Jalen Hurts and a second, and Hurts is on IR. Trevor Lawrence and a second went out for Lamar Jackson, who lasted one snap in Week 8. DJ Moore went the other way for Tyler Goodson and a 2029 second, which at least sounds like a rebuild. So the rebuilding team swapped two younger quarterbacks for one on IR and one who played a single snap last Sunday. I can talk myself into it: it's a buy-low, and superflex quarterbacks never go out of style. I can also picture a guy buying two used Porsches the week he swore he was saving for a house. The house is still there: four 2027 firsts, though the ones from Jeantrification, the Church and Shough My Hock all project late. Meanwhile both running back seats are below replacement, and it's 2-6 and eleventh in Elo. Pick a lane, because right now this is neither.

5.head: 1-7 · Elo 1258 (12th) · WAR pace +0.37 (12th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
5.text: Finally, a win! Against Tyson chicken tenders, the only other 1-7 team, which in a race to the bottom is like Antoine Walker shimmying after a three when you're down twenty. This team was never about this season and it's playing the part: last in Elo, last in WAR pace, and a roster where Mike Gesicki and Sam Darnold lead in banked WAR at 0.22 apiece. That's not a stat line, it's a cry for help. Marvin Harrison is on the bench on pace for -0.42 WAR, Jeremiyah Love is on pace for 0.17 as a rookie, and the Vele trade brought back CJ Donaldson, who is on IR. None of it matters next to the draft board: four 2027 firsts, its own plus Drake Mungo's, Homie G's and Hampton Inn's, then three 2028 firsts and its own 2029. Hampton Inn's could land early, and its own could land first. Nobody in the league has more ammo. Patience until April, then this becomes the most interesting team in the league.

12.head: 1-7 · Elo 1310 (10th) · WAR pace +1.01 (10th) · playoffs 0% · title 0%
12.text: The tenders are 1-7, last in points, and starting Brenton Strange at superflex. Read that again: a tight end in the quarterback seat, because Jaxson Dart, the one guy who was producing, is on IR along with Jordyn Tyson, Jayden Higgins, Terrance Ferguson and De'Zhaun Stribling. Baker Mayfield is below replacement for the season, and so is TreVeyon Henderson. Harold Fannin and Jameson Williams lead the roster with 0.32 and 0.29 WAR banked, which tells you how dark it is in here. The front office did the hard part right: Saquon Barkley sold for Brian Thomas and a second, Bucky Irving sold for a 2028 first, both before the value evaporated. The catch is Thomas, who is on pace for -0.56 WAR. Two 2027 firsts, its own and the Nix pics' (who are sliding, which helps), plus two extra 2027 seconds. Grab any warm-body quarterback off waivers so the superflex isn't a tight end, then go back to collecting.
